newsitem.title: FRANCE: Bouygues says Cise-Saur may be listed.
newsitem.headline: Bouygues says Cise-Saur may be listed.

text.p: French building group Bouygues may list the merged Cise-Saur entity "around 1999", chairman Martin Bouygues said in an interview with financial weekly Investir.
Bouygues' Saur unit acquired public contract management firm Cise from glassmaker Saint-Gobain last year.
Martin Bouygues also said the Bouygues Telecom unit might be listed "in coming years".
Asked whether Bouygues might seek to acquire another group in the building sector, such as GTM-Entrepose, he said, "We do not envisage getting closer to GTM-Entrepose".
He added that he believed the restructuring of the building and public works sector was largely complete.
Bouygues also said he expected the industry to benefit if the new Socialist-led government focused on job creation.

"Building and public works is one of the big industrial sectors that has suffered for several years and one of the biggest employers. We would imagine that policies favouring employment would take its difficulties into account...The effects of a recovery in this all-French industry would greatly benefit the national economy," he was quoted as saying.
Bouygues said a delay or cancellation of the partial privatisation of France Telecom "would be felt on public finances, but would change nothing for our profession and for our group".
Referring to the cable business, he said the group was continuing discussions with Lyonnaise des Eaux "which could conclude with an agreement before the end of the year".
Elsewhere, he said turnover in the Asia-Pacific region should total around six billion francs this year, with roughly half coming from private contracts.
